title: Columbia River flood basalts
summary: The Columbia River Basalt Group erupted more than 350 lava flows between about 16.7 and 5.5 million years ago, most of its volume in about 1.1 million years from 16.7 to 15.6 Ma. Fissures along the Washington–Oregon–Idaho border fed flows that often exceeded 1,000 km3 and now cover over 210,000 km2 of eastern Oregon and Washington, western Idaho and northern Nevada.

uncertainty.note: Range is the main phase named by USGS (about 16.7 to 15.6 Ma); the whole group erupted from about 16.7 to 5.5 Ma (USGS) or 17.5 to 6 Ma (Lewis and Clark Trail Alliance). Jarboe et al. (2010) date the Steens reversal at 16.73 +0.13/-0.08 Ma. Years are Ma with no 1950 offset.

when.display: c. 16.7–15.6 million years ago (group erupted to c. 5.5 Ma)

where.modern_name: Steens Mountain, Oregon (dated lava flows; the province spans eastern Oregon and Washington, western Idaho and northern Nevada)
where.historical_name: Interior Pacific Northwest of North America, Miocene; no polities

importance.justification: A large Miocene flood-basalt province in the western United States.
